basis: Neuroendocrine neoplasm arising in the bronchus; functional hormonal syndromes and cardiac or hepatic injury are very rare.
HMBS-related metabolic encephalopathy; cataracts in 2/3, anemia in 1/3 with splenomegaly in 2/3; kyphosis omitted at cap; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver injury.
Epithelial neoplasm located in the colon.
Immune-mediated injury of peripheral motor axons defines this Guillain-Barre subtype; weakness reflects denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
Bilateral congenital duplication and fusion of digits; nonsyndromic skeletal malformation.
Platelet bleeding, neutropenic immunodeficiency and cutaneous albinism define HPS2; visual impairment affects most; pulmonary disease omitted under the four-axis cap.
Structural dental anomaly affecting molar pulp chambers and roots; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Autoinflammatory small-vessel vasculopathy with destructive skin lesions; pulmonary fibrosis in 6/10; myositis in 2/5 and muscle atrophy in 2/6 omitted at cap.
Peripheral nerve injury caused by uremia from kidney failure; both renal dysfunction and neuropathy define the condition.
Glycogen synthesis disorder specifically affecting skeletal muscle and myocardium, with myopathy and potentially severe cardiac dysfunction; seizures are occasional.
Visceral heterotaxy subtype associated with congenital heart malformations; abnormal abdominal organ positioning alone does not establish organ damage.
Invasive adenocarcinoma arising in colonic epithelium.
Adenoviral infection defined by pharyngitis and conjunctivitis; pharyngeal and conjunctival inflammation are primary disease sites.
Sarcoma of the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes; mesenchymal histology does not imply locomotor involvement.
XP/Cockayne overlap combines photodermatosis and neurodevelopmental degeneration; damaging ocular disease and sensorineural hearing loss are common, approximately >=30%.
Neoplasm arising in the fallopian tube, outside the axes; resemblance to gastrointestinal epithelium does not indicate gastrointestinal origin.
Inherited coagulation-factor deficiency; hemarthroses are frequent (30-79%) and can directly injure joints; epistaxis alone does not establish airway damage.
Idiopathic resorption and osteonecrosis of phalangeal bone.
Primary skeletal dysplasia affecting ulnar and other metaphyses; dental abnormalities and kidney stones are occasional (5-29%).
Familial vesicoureteral reflux affects the bladder-ureter junction and urinary tract; infections are separate complications.
Alagille bile-duct paucity and congenital cardiovascular defects; butterfly vertebrae in roughly 50%, renal anomalies in roughly 40%; posterior embryotoxon usually non-damaging.
OTOA-related nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no additional organ disease is established.
Immune-mediated necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis; visceral distribution alone does not establish common damage to any particular additional organ.
Malignancy involving the tonsillar oropharynx, within the pharyngeal airway axis; lymphoma is only one subtype of this umbrella concept.
Adenocarcinoma arising in nasal cavity glandular epithelium; the nasal airway belongs to the pulmonary axis.
